clean_story:
Artificial sound creation. Music from mathematics.

The term sound synthesis comes from combining "sound" and "synthesis," meaning to build sound from simpler parts, like assembling a puzzle from individual pieces. Most sounds in nature are complex waves, but synthesis breaks them into pure tones—like sine waves—and reassembles them into new shapes. A piano note is a mix of frequencies; synthesis isolates these, then stacks them to craft entirely new timbres. Early analog synthesizers, like the RCA Mark II in 1957, used oscillators to generate raw waveforms, which were then sculpted with filters and envelopes. Today, digital synthesis lets a laptop mimic an orchestra or invent sounds no instrument could produce. A video game’s laser blast or a sci-fi movie’s alien hum likely started as a synthesized wave, shaped by a designer’s precise adjustments.
Three related subjects are wave modulation, electronic music, and how sound shapes emotion.
